Mixed-Use Property Loans

Underwriting

What we look at on a mixed-use loan

  • The split between commercial and residential space, and the income from each
  • Commercial lease terms: length, renewals and who pays expenses
  • The residential rent roll and occupancy
  • Zoning and the permitted uses for each floor
  • Whether you'll occupy the commercial space yourself
Scenarios

Common mixed-use deals we see

  • Buying a downtown building with a café below and four apartments above
  • A business owner buying the building their shop operates from and renting the units upstairs
  • Refinancing a renovated mixed-use building to pull out equity
Mixed-Use loan FAQ

Common questions about mixed-use loans.

Can my business operate in a mixed-use building I finance with SLA Capital?

Yes. Owner-occupied commercial is eligible: a business can buy or refinance the building it operates from. These are business-purpose loans, so ask your loan officer if you also plan to live in one of the units.

How do you value a building with both retail and apartments?

We look at the income from each space and at the building as a whole, with an appraisal that accounts for both uses.

Can I finance a mixed-use building with vacant storefronts?

Yes. That's a bridge-loan scenario: buy, renovate and lease up, then refinance into a commercial DSCR loan once the building is stabilized.

What loan sizes are available for mixed-use property?

Commercial bridge loans up to $20,000,000 and commercial DSCR loans up to $3,000,000, each reviewed and priced case by case.
